title: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic Explored Own AI Testing Due to Federal Resource Gaps

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The companies behind the most prominent large language models considered creating an independent evaluation unit as they grew dissatisfied with the Commerce Department's testing agency. Google, OpenAI and Anthropic explored forming a private group to vet frontier AI models because they believe the federal government lacks the resources and staff to conduct adequate assessments, according to The Information.

The move comes as the White House intends to shift three senior officials from the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI) into the executive office to report to science adviser Michael Kratsios and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross. CAISSI currently operates with about 40 staff and an annual budget of $10 million to $15 million, with maximum salaries capped at $174,000. This is the agency's third organizational shake-up in less than 2 years.

Scoop: The small agency within the Commerce Department tasked with testing new AI models, CAISSI, is getting its long-awaited refresh. 

The Trump administration recently finalized a plan to have three senior CAISSI officials report directly to the White House to better streamline the agency, which has long been plagued by resource and access issues. 

However, there has been confusion between the White House and Commerce Department on the restructure, which a White House official told me demonstrates why CAISSI leadership needs to move. 

Lots of new details here, including the debate over how to manage CAISSI, its role in the White House's AI framework for testing AI models, and personnel changes

selectedTweets.text:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: Trump is moving 3 senior officials from CAISSI, the government's AI testing agency, into the White House.

• They'll report to Michael Kratsios and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, after coordination problems with Commerce
• It's the agency's 3rd shake-up in under 2 years, from Biden's AI Safety Institute to Trump's CAISI to today's CAISSI
• It runs on about 40 staff and $15M a year, less than some individual researchers at AI labs make
• Its staff work from NIST's Gaithersburg campus, 45 minutes outside DC, for at most $174K a year instead of lab equity in SF
• Many in the administration see it as too "doomer," so moving its officials into the White House reads as a vote of confidence
• The administration already runs an unofficial pre-deployment testing program: labs share models, get feedback, and get asked to delay or cleared to launch

@theojaffee: "Famously, CAISSI's budget annually is like $10 to $15 million a year in total. That's the entire department budget. There are individual researchers at labs who make more money than that in a year."

selectedTweets.text:
Trump is reportedly bringing Super Intelligence testing closer to the White House. Reuters, citing The Information, reports that three senior officials from CAISSI, the agency assessing advanced AI models, are set to move from the Commerce Department to the White House.

They would report to science adviser Michael Kratsios and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross. The stated goal is to resolve coordination problems and bring model evaluations directly into the administration's AI decision-making.

That would put assessments of frontier capabilities closer to the people shaping national policy, with a stronger link to cybersecurity leadership. The move remains unconfirmed publicly; neither the White House nor Commerce responded to Reuters' request for comment.
